Subject: Post-call recap: Access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap from our call focused on access controls for customer data and next steps we discussed: 

- Key asks from you: RBAC (least-privilege for end-users & admins), fine-grained support access (audited "break-glass"), session and query logging, and data residency in us-east-1.
- What Redwood can provide: role-based permission model, scoped API keys/service accounts, admin vs. support vs. read-only role templates, and an auditable support access flow (temporary escalation with full session logging).
- Items you asked for: an RBAC matrix (role -> allowed actions + data scoping), a draft break-glass runbook showing approval flow and audit trail, and our SOC 2 attestation and data retention summary.

I've attached a short RBAC-summary.pdf that outlines the role templates we typically use and a draft break-glass runbook (support-break-glass-process.docx). Also dropping in the HubSpot deal + a Drive folder where we'll upload more artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share the RBAC matrix + break-glass runbook (attached).
2) Schedule a 30-45 minute architecture review next week to walk through how roles map to your org and how support access would be gated.
3) Share SOC2 and retention policy docs in the Drive folder.

Possible times: Tue 8/10 10:00-11:00 or Wed 8/11 14:00-15:00 PT - let me know what works for you and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintrust.com>

Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the recap - that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: must be in us-east-1. We need assurance that customer data never leaves that region for processing or backups.
- RBAC: we need roles that can be scoped to customer org units and to specific datasets (so that a tenant admin can only see their own data).
- Support access / break-glass: support should be able to request temporary elevated access (max 1 hour), must be approved by our on-call, and every session must be recorded and stored for 180 days.
- Logging: query-level logs are required for auditing (retention 180 days) and we need the ability to export logs to our SIEM.

If your attachments include a draft RBAC matrix and the runbook, that will be super helpful. Also please confirm whether Redwood supports exporting logs to a customer-owned Cloud Storage endpoint.

Priya (cc) will help coordinate an internal security review.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure, FinTrust
alex.turner@fintrust.com

Looping in engineering/infra to confirm capabilities. A couple of quick notes / questions from our side before the architecture review: 

- RBAC matrix: we support resource-scoped roles (tenant, dataset, model) and attribute-based scoping (e.g., tag-based dataset filters). Will create a concrete matrix mapping common roles to actions (read/generate/admin/agent).
- Support break-glass: we have a temporary elevation flow that uses pre-approved SSO groups + short-lived tokens. We can enable session recording and route logs to a customer-owned GCS/S3 bucket; need the specific account/bucket details and IAM role.
- Retention & export: logs/queries can be retained in Redwood for 180 days (configurable) and we can export via streaming to a customer endpoint. Export requires a one-time config step (service role + destination).

Marissa - I'll draft the RBAC matrix and a short runbook showing the approval flow + what is recorded (commands, session transcript, requester, approver, timestamps). Dev - can you prepare a short diagram of how the session elevates and how audit logs are captured?

Rishi
